name: Montecito
summary: Oak-shaded lanes, walled estates and two villages with the best coffee on the South Coast.
body: Montecito runs from the foothills to Butterfly Beach. Lower Village and Upper Village each have their own character, and the lanes between them are lined with century-old oaks and stone walls. Most sales here are private estates on an acre or more.

name: Hope Ranch
summary: A gated enclave with its own beach, bridle trails and a lagoon at the center.
body: Hope Ranch is a private community west of the city with roughly 750 homes, a members-only beach and miles of riding trails. Lots are large, often an acre or more, and the architecture is a mix of mid-century ranches and new contemporary houses.

name: The Riviera
summary: Switchback lanes on the hillside above the Old Mission, with views over the city to the harbor.
body: The Riviera climbs the hill behind the Old Mission. Houses here date mostly from the 1920s and 1930s, and nearly all of them have a view. It is quiet, walkable and a few minutes from downtown.

name: The Mesa
summary: A flat coastal bluff of family streets, surf breaks and sunset walks along Shoreline Park.
body: The Mesa sits on a bluff between the harbor and Hendry's Beach. It is the most neighborly part of town, with small cafés, good schools and the long clifftop path of Shoreline Park.

name: Downtown
summary: Condominiums and townhouses within walking distance of State Street, the Arlington and the Funk Zone.
body: Downtown Santa Barbara has a small but growing supply of condominiums and townhouses, most of them built in the last decade. Residents walk to restaurants, theaters and the Saturday farmers market.

name: Mission Canyon
summary: Wooded canyon lots above the Botanic Garden, with trailheads at the end of the street.
body: Mission Canyon follows the creek up from the Old Mission into the foothills. Lots are wooded and private, and the hiking trails start at the top of the canyon.

name: Summerland
summary: A hillside beach village of porches, antiques shops and ocean views.
body: Summerland is a tiny village between Montecito and Carpinteria. Its streets climb the hill above the freeway, so nearly every house has a view of the water, and the beach is reached by a short set of steps from Lookout Park.

name: Carpinteria
summary: A relaxed beach town with the calmest swimming beach on the coast.
body: Carpinteria calls itself the world's safest beach, and the reef offshore keeps the water calm. The town is relaxed and walkable, with a strong local school district and a growing restaurant scene.

name: Ojai
summary: A valley town of citrus groves, craftsman houses and the Pink Moment at dusk.
body: Ojai is forty minutes inland, in a valley ringed by mountains. The East End holds most of the older craftsman and ranch properties, many on an acre or more of citrus and oak.
